issues.description: The dark thumb-root hollow in the -35 deg view comes from the D22 thumb-CMC move, and the report does not say so. openIssues says only 'The crease was already there at HEAD. The old slit-like fold is now a shaded hollow'. Moving the CMC back shortens the home-view fold (74 -> ~47 px), but in yawm35 the step-3 slit opens into a dark triangular pit behind the thumb MCP. The thumb then reads as plugged into the palm. The trend is monotonic in the CMC depth: z 0.24 gives a slit and no pit; z 0.20 a smaller pit and a ~70 px fold; z 0.17 (committed) the full pit and a ~47 px fold. It does not come from the palm thinning: the step-3 palm with z 0.17 still has the pit. All three depths pass every gate. D22 directs this move and the calibrator applied it within D22's range, so a fixer must not change it. I list it so the main session knows what D22 costs in the -35 deg view. It matters little for the particle hand's home view.

issues.description: The report blames the reversed knuckle arch on the builder, but a pose edit reaches a modest convex arch. The middle MCP sits 2.6 mm palmar of the index-ring line. openIssues says 'Arch variants cost 0.25 px mean ... and left ring-little root voids'. The void-filling builder request says it 'would also let the pose put the knuckles on a convex arch without chasing voids'. That holds for the calibrator's A1/A2 variants, not in general. XD passes every gate, A1 (1 shell) and D9, and puts the middle knuckle highest: +1.33 mm against index +0.64, ring -0.58, little -1.39. It moves only middle_mcp 4.5 mm dorsally and pinky_mcp 2 mm palmar; mean +0.057 px, p95 7.616 -> 8.0. The difference is subtle in the above view. XD left the middle PIP where it was, so the middle P1 grew 44.7 -> 48.3 mm; a real edit would re-solve that finger's hinge plane. Optional anatomy polish, not a blocker.
